property_summary: After a call to Collect, the unlockTime for any account is never less than block.timestamp.
After a Collect call that succeeds, the unlockTime of the caller is always at least block.timestamp.
After a call to Collect, the balance of the caller is never decreased by more than the amount requested.

The unlock time condition prevents Collect from succeeding before the unlock time, meaning that if Collect succeeds (does not revert), then block.timestamp must be greater than the unlock time at the time of the call.
After any Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is exactly the same as before the call, because Put is never called during Collect.
After a call to Collect, the contract's balance is never negative (i.e., the sum of all account balances does not exceed the total ether balance of the contract).
After Collect, msg.sender's balance in the contract is never greater than the contract's entire ether balance.
After Collect, the total balance of all holders (sum of Acc[].balance) equals the contract's ether balance minus the sum of ether sent out in Collect calls.
After a successful Collect call, the sum of all account balances in the contract does not decrease compared to before the call.
After any call to Collect, the contract's ether balance is at least the sum of all account balances.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the contract's balance equals the sum of its account balances.
After any call to Collect, the total Ether held by the contract equals the sum of all user balances recorded in the Acc mapping.
After a Collect call from user1, the contract's total Ether balance equals the sum of the balances of all users' accounts.
After a Collect call where the caller has sufficient balance and time, the caller's balance decreases by exactly the amount sent.

After a call to Collect(amount) that reverts, the contract's total balance equals the sum of all Acc balances, and if it does not revert, the sum of Acc balances decreases by exactly amount (plus transfer costs already factored).
After any call to Collect(uint256), the Collect function never reverts when the caller's balance is at least MinSum and the caller's unlockTime has passed.
After Collect(uint256) returns without reverting, the contract balance remains at least MinSum.
After a non-reverting Collect(uint256) call, the sum of all user balances in Acc mapping equals the contract's ether balance.
After any successful Collect call, the balance of the caller in the Acc mapping never exceeds the contract's ether balance minus MinSum.
After Collect is called, the total sum of Acc balances never exceeds the contract's ether balance.
Collect should only allow withdrawal of the exact full balance when _am equals acc.balance, but the buggy version reverts when _am equals acc.balance due to using > instead of >=.
Collect should succeed when _am equals acc.balance, but the buggy version reverts when _am equals acc.balance due to using > instead of >=.
Collect(uint256) always succeeds when _am equals the caller's current balance, regardless of other conditions.
Collect always returns the full transfer amount to the caller when _am equals their balance.
Collect should succeed when _am equals the caller's balance (acc.balance >= _am), but the buggy version requires acc.balance > _am, causing revert when _am equals acc.balance.
